title: Artifact byte checksums
text: API: md5 gives the exact contract. artifact_checksum::md5 computes the sixteen MD5 digest bytes for a byte slice. The artifact parser uses this legacy checksum for its Z-card check. The Z card is the artifact checksum record. It does not select repository content identities. SHA-1 and SHA3 remain in content_hash. Structural parsing has its own explicit limits and validation rules. Md5Checksum::new starts an owned computation. update appends the complete slice, including zero bytes and bytes outside UTF-8. Empty updates do nothing. finish consumes the computation and returns [u8; 16]. Each value has fixed memory use and can be interleaved with other computations. No input copy, file access or process-global state is required. Slice lengths bound each call. The caller chooses how much data to supply. There is no artifact size policy or cancellation mechanism in this byte primitive. use gossil::artifact_checksum::{md5, Md5Checksum}; let mut checksum = Md5Checksum::new(); checksum.update(b"a"); checksum.update(b"bc"); assert_eq!(checksum.finish(), md5(b"abc"));

title: Artifact byte checksums
text: The inspected Fossil mirror is b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The native build reports 7e8ecf0ce4a3c05aa39de7ffe2828d23e334efe446ef2387e09f205ef00b2227. In src/manifest.c, verify_z_card hashes the bytes before the final 35-byte Z card through md5sum_init, md5sum_step_text and md5sum_finish. This module supplies that checksum operation. It does not inspect a Z card. The byte result maps to md5sum_blob in src/md5.c. The incremental operations map to the positive-length and zero-length byte behavior of md5sum_step_text. Rust ownership replaces the native shared context and overwritten static result. The consuming finish requires a fresh value for another computation. It does not reproduce the native implicit reset. Negative lengths and C string scanning are excluded. md5sum_step_blob needs no separate Rust adapter because slices already describe bytes and length. Excluded native functions are md5sum_current_state, md5sum_file and md5sum_test. md5sum_current_state sums words of the internal context for troubleshooting. Its two callers in vfile.c are commented out. It is not a snapshot of the MD5 digest. The native command and filesystem behaviors, repository R-card aggregation, ETags and all artifact producers remain outside this module. Native MD5Init, MD5Update, MD5Final, MD5Transform and DigestToBase16 are not translated into Rust here. The implementation uses RustCrypto’s exact-pinned md-5 version 0.10.6. This version shares the existing digest 0.10 dependency with SHA-2. The lockfile records its registry checksum. Its versioned documentation describes the API used here. RustCrypto’s current documentation identifies legacy interoperability as the purpose of MD5. This module adds no identity or security policy and forwards no computation to C.

title: Artifact parser
text: API: parse_artifact gives the exact contract. The artifact module parses all eight Fossil structural artifact types with explicit resource limits. The types are manifest, cluster, control, wiki, ticket, attachment, technote and forum. A card is a record in the artifact byte format. The parser takes bytes and returns an owned result with read-only access to parsed fields. It keeps the original input, including any signature envelope. It does not require valid UTF-8.

title: Artifact parser
text: Call parse_artifact(input, limits, dates).await with a ParseLimits value chosen for the calling operation. Set each field explicitly, including input_bytes, cards, owned_bytes and entries. All four fields have type usize. The byte fields count bytes, and the other fields count cards and list entries. There is no default policy. The owned-byte limit counts retained input, token allocations and list entries. Allocations use fallible reservation. A resource failure is separate from malformed input, checksum mismatch and a date-provider failure. Implement DateProvider on the operation’s selected SQLite/libSQL owner. Its asynchronous julianday method can borrow a transaction. It receives an optional raw token already truncated by the parser at its native C-string boundary, and returns an optional Julian day. A NULL result acts as zero and fails date validation. Provider execution errors retain their original cause. A constant date adapter can isolate grammar tests, but it cannot qualify date compatibility. The result exposes decoded comments and users, manifest files and parents, tags, ticket fields and cluster members. It also exposes attachment fields, wiki and forum fields, body bytes and converted dates. D cards carry artifact dates, and E cards carry event dates. Their raw date tokens remain available. Callers cannot construct or mutate a validated result through this API.

title: Artifact parser
text: The port follows Fossil manifest.c:467-1153 and its eight allowed/required card masks at lines 129-138. The pinned Fossil UUID is 7e8ecf0ce4a3c05aa39de7ffe2828d23e334efe446ef2387e09f205ef00b2227. Fossil’s source is copyright D. Richard Hipp under the Simplified BSD License. The parser checks the exact MD5 before decoding a recognized final Z record. It strips recognized PGP and SSH envelopes for parsing and checksum purposes. Envelope stripping does not verify a signature’s authenticity. The pinned card matrix requires Z even for manifests. R validates hexadecimal syntax. Repository file checksum verification belongs to storage. Tokens stop at space, LF or raw NUL. Each card consumes tokens as its native branch does. A raw NUL can be an intermediate delimiter in some cards. It is not subject to a blanket acceptance rule. Decoded tokens retain bytes after an escaped NUL, together with the length visible to C consumers. A zero card marker ends the native card loop after consuming its space or LF delimiter. Parsing succeeds only if that cursor reaches the end and the earlier cards satisfy the type rules. Unread bytes after the marker still fail. The W scanner uses unsigned 32-bit modular arithmetic and the native new < old overflow branch. It checks the remaining input before copying body bytes. Decimal suffixes and empty digit sequences follow the source branch. Manifest file paths use the legacy nonstrict rules. Paths must be nonempty and have no empty, dot or dot-dot slash-separated components. Unicode and backslash restrictions are not imposed. Reserved filenames are suppressed after comparison with the last retained filename. The parser retains repeated empty P cards, native type inference, tag ordering, forum postconditions and the historical technote P-before-N exception. Attachment basenames follow the compiled platform’s directory separator rule. Windows behavior remains unqualified.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: API: pack gives the exact contract. The library has Fossil byte digests and packed-blob operations. Packing adds a capacity header to compressed bytes. These primitives do not select a repository hash policy or store content. The runner and these primitives share a crate. CLI integration remains separate work. Legacy MD5 checksums have a separate artifact checksum module. The artifact parser uses that module for Z-card validation. The checksum module does not select repository content identities.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: use gossil::{compression, content_hash}; let digest = content_hash::sha1(b"abc"); assert_eq!(digest.len(), 20); let packed = compression::pack(b"abc", -1).unwrap(); assert_eq!(compression::unpack(&packed, 3).unwrap(), compression::Unpacked::Bytes(b"abc".to_vec())); In the example, -1 selects the default compression level, and 3 limits decoded output to three bytes. sha1(input: &[u8]) returns [u8; 20]. pack(input: &[u8], level: i32) returns Result , BlobError>. unpack(input: &[u8], max_output: usize) returns Result . See the runner prerequisites for actual tool setup.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: The port follows Fossil Git revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The source surfaces are src/blob.c:1372–1535, src/sha1.c:185–201, and src/sha3.c:385–468,591–606,622–679, and the SHA1DC initialization in src/sha1hard.c:1327–1342. content_hash::sha1 accepts arbitrary bytes and returns twenty digest bytes. SHA1DC detects known SHA1 collision attacks. It preserves Fossil’s collision detection and safe-hash defaults. For a known collision attack, it returns the mitigated digest. The byte helper ignores the separate collision indication, as sha1sum_blob does. It does not return the ordinary vulnerable digest for those inputs. content_hash::sha3 accepts each width from 128 through 512 in steps of 32. It returns the corresponding binary digest, or None for an unsupported width. content_hash::hex renders bytes as lowercase hexadecimal. SHA3 uses Fossil’s width-dependent capacity and its 0x06 and 0x80 padding. The small adapter handles byte absorption, padding and extraction in explicit little-endian lane order. The maintained keccak crate supplies the permutation. A shorter digest is not a truncated standard-width hash. The four standard widths use FIPS-202 padding. The other widths preserve Fossil’s extensions. compression::pack accepts zlib levels -1 and zero through nine. Level -1 selects the backend default. compression::pack_two compresses the concatenated slices at level nine, as Fossil does. Neither operation allocates a concatenated input buffer. The compressed representation can differ between backends. A packed blob contains a four-byte unsigned big-endian capacity followed by a zlib stream. The capacity is an upper bound on decoded bytes. A larger header than the actual output is valid. Bytes following the first complete zlib stream are ignored. Invalid checksums, incomplete streams and output exceeding the header produce errors. compression::unpack accepts a caller-selected limit. It rejects a header above that limit before decoding, then checks each output chunk against the header. Output grows through fallible reservations. The caller sets the limit. The format has no additional fixed small cap. Encoding rejects lengths above the unsigned 32-bit header range. C overflow and undefined behavior are not ported. Inputs of at most four bytes produce Unpacked::NoPayload. A caller that replaces an existing buffer must leave its existing buffer contents unchanged for that result. A successfully decoded empty stream produces Unpacked::Bytes with an empty vector. These outcomes differ. Fossil’s diagnostic test-uncompress ignores the C function’s error return, so CLI exit zero does not prove successful decoding. Allocation and compression errors retain their underlying causes. Digest results have a fixed small size. Compressed input and output remain caller-owned. The API does not define database, filesystem, publication or privacy behavior.

title: CLI reference
text: The gossil executable has three file diagnostics. Each command runs without a repository. Run it from this source checkout with just gossil, which builds and runs the executable through Cargo. Cargo may print build messages on stderr. Command Arguments Successful output vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA Writes DELTA; no stdout vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Writes TARGET; no stdout vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Prints ok and a newline just gossil vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA just gossil vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET just gossil vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Replace capitalized arguments with file paths. The commands accept exactly the number of paths shown. There are no root aliases or help subcommands. File data comes from paths and goes to paths. Stdin and stdout do not carry it.

title: CLI reference
text: Success returns status 0. Usage, input, delta and output failures return status 1 with one diagnostic line on stderr. Missing input reports no such file: PATH. An output-open failure reports unable to open file "PATH" for writing. Invalid delta application reports Delta application failed.. A failed round trip reports delta test failed. Create and apply read their inputs before opening the output. This permits an output path to name an input file. Input or validation failures preserve an existing output, but an output write failure can leave it truncated. Parent folders must already exist. The encoder guide and decoder guide describe format bounds and the library errors behind these diagnostics. The getting started example uses distinct output files.

title: CLI reference
text: gossil-conformance is a separate development executable. It runs one explicit inherited-test configuration through just conformance CONFIG. It does not implement a Gossil engine. Its configuration, prerequisites and acceptance rules are in the runner guide.

title: Library concepts
text: Gossil separates byte operations, artifact structure and local database ownership. A byte operation does not create a repository, and a parsed artifact does not establish its place in a repository graph.

title: Library concepts
text: The delta module creates and applies Fossil deltas. Application takes an explicit output limit. The compression module packs and unpacks blobs, which are stored byte sequences. Unpacking also takes a decoded size limit. The content_hash module computes content digests. A digest identifies bytes. It does not grant access to those bytes. The artifact_checksum module computes legacy MD5 checksums for artifact records. It does not choose the repository’s content hash policy.

title: Library concepts
text: The token_codec module escapes byte values for Fossil record tokens. Its byte and C-string forms have different zero-byte behavior. The token guide defines those contracts. The artifact module parses eight structural artifact types with explicit limits. A caller supplies the date provider, which converts date fields. Parsing checks structure and checksums. Repository graph validation requires more storage rules. See the parser guide.

title: Library concepts
text: LocalStore owns a local libSQL connection and one exclusive write transaction. A transaction must commit or roll back before the connection returns to the store. The public interface does not expose arbitrary SQL. LocalOwnerRepository initializes a complete empty public root. It also supports bounded private content operations. The empty root is a check-in with no files. A private content write does not create a file-containing check-in. Admission validates the stored root before repository operations. SharedView restricts access to admitted public content. Operating-system access establishes local owner authority. The native storage guide defines admission, content bounds and access rules. General crosslinks, sync and team authentication remain planned.

title: Library concepts
text: Gest is a task and artifact tracker. These converters use its task and project record model. The gest_task_values module validates eleven already decoded task fields. It returns an owned record with canonical status and UTC timestamps. The task values guide defines validation and caller responsibilities. The gest_project_values module validates the four canonical project fields, gest_id, archived_at, created_at and updated_at. It returns an owned record with an identifier, nullable archive time and UTC timestamps. The project values guide defines the complete field contract. A local checkout root is outside the canonical project record. Raw input admission, storage integration and task or project commands remain separate work.

title: Library concepts
text: Choose the smallest module that fits the operation. Next, set resource limits at every decoding or parsing boundary and read that module’s error contract.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: gossil-conformance executes one Fossil Tcl suite against an explicit program. It is development infrastructure and implements no Gossil engine behavior. A reference run tests the pinned upstream Fossil program. A candidate run tests the replacement program whose compatibility is under development. The runs have separate configurations and output directories. A missing candidate never falls back to C Fossil. Run just conformance-self-test to check the runner controls. These tests pass when the runner correctly rejects deliberate failures and incomplete runs. That result does not mean the inherited Fossil suites pass.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Install Rust with Cargo, Git, Just and uv on PATH before using the recipes. Rust builds the runner, Just runs Justfile recipes, and uv runs the installed workflow tools. just setup fetches Cargo dependencies. just install --check checks the saved workflow installation rather than supplying native test tools. This checkout exposes Tcl 8.6.18 and Fossil 2.29 through .jlog/bin. The Fossil binary is revision 7e8ecf0ce4, with TLS and FUSE disabled. These ignored tools are local prerequisites. A fresh clone does not acquire them, so continuous integration from a fresh clone remains unproved. Supply the pinned Fossil source and native tools yourself before running reference suites. The repository has no automated acquisition procedure. The user temporarily permitted the local Tcl installation to use shared Homebrew storage rather than keeping all native dependencies inside the checkout.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Write a JSON configuration with absolute paths. The following example uses the checked-in positive control. Replace /path/to/gossil with the checkout path. The output directory must not exist. Save this example as CONFIG.json. { "role": "reference", "revision": "b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6", "tcl": "/path/to/gossil/.jlog/bin/tclsh", "driver": "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/controls/tester.tcl", "executable": "/path/to/gossil/.jlog/bin/fossil", "suite": "pass", "run_dir": "/path/to/gossil/target/conformance/example", "timeout_ms": 3000, "seed": 20261117, "inputs": [ "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/fossil/tester.tcl", "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/fossil/enable.patch" ], "capabilities": {"tls": "disabled", "fuse": "disabled"} }

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Field Meaning and effect role Required label reference or candidate. It does not select a binary. revision Nonempty source identifier retained in evidence. The runner does not verify a source checkout against it. tcl Absolute path to an executable Tcl interpreter. driver Absolute path to the enabled tester.tcl driver. executable Absolute path to the program under test, used without fallback. suite Suite basename without a slash, for example pass for pass.test. run_dir Absolute path to a new output directory whose parent already exists. timeout_ms Positive deadline in milliseconds. A timeout rejects the run. seed Unsigned 32-bit value passed to Tcl srand before the driver runs. It controls Tcl randomness, not every source of randomness in the tested program. inputs Absolute paths to extra source, fixture or patch files whose bytes need hashing. capabilities Caller-supplied string map retained as evidence. It neither enables features nor verifies their availability. invocation_plan Optional complete plan and corpus pins; omitted or null uses strict duplicate-name rejection. See the plan contract below. The runner locates  .test beside driver. The example runs tests/fixtures/controls/pass.test. For an upstream suite, keep the original source tree and corpus unchanged. Put a copy of tester.tcl and the selected suite beside each other in a separate harness directory. Apply tests/fixtures/fossil/enable.patch only to the copied driver. Prepend set argv0 /absolute/path/to/original/test/tester.tcl to that enabled copy, using the original driver path in the pinned source tree. This restores the original corpus location when the driver derives testdir from argv0. Set driver to the enabled copy. The executed delta1 harness uses this layout; its original driver, suite and corpus bytes remain unchanged. The runner hashes the driver, suite, interpreter and tested executable automatically, in addition to every path in inputs. The example’s revision is the Git mirror commit for the inherited source. Fossil identifies the same source snapshot with its native revision, starting 7e8ecf0ce4. The full pair and driver hashes are in the repository file evidence/baselines/fossil/provenance.json. The label alone does not prove that an executable was built from that source. Create the parent output folder, then run just conformance CONFIG.json. Exit status 0 means this suite passed, status 1 means it failed acceptance, and status 2 means setup failed. The runner prints the report.json path. The report retains decoded stdout and stderr, commands, environment, hashes, source pin, suite, original assertion names, seed, capabilities and process status. The log files retain exact bytes and their hashes. Invalid UTF-8 blocks acceptance. Only stdout supplies assertion records, while stderr remains evidence. Without a plan, assertion identity combines the source pin, suite path and original name. The runner does not infer parameterized cases or unreported seeds. Callers must supply all fixture and source inputs that need hashing. Framework checks remain separate from real assertions. Known-bug annotations remain visible, but an assertion reported as failing never becomes a pass. Skipped summaries produce not-run with the original reason. The runner has no automatic feature-disabled mapping. A separate analysis must link the skipped reason to a capability observation, as the reference archive described in evidence/baselines/README.md does. The configuration map alone does not establish that classification. Timeouts and incomplete output produce blocked. Only pass contributes to acceptance. A skip or blocked result prevents acceptance of the entire suite, even if other assertions pass. A framework-only run fails acceptance. The runner also rejects missing summaries, inconsistent counts and crashes. For example, the final summary for one passing assertion is ***** Final results: 0 errors out of 1 tests. A final summary invalidates the run if a count is nonnumeric or exceeds the range of usize, Rust’s unsigned pointer-sized integer type. Every final-summary occurrence counts, including malformed ones. A duplicate summary or a later valid summary cannot clear that rejection.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: The default parser rejects repeated original assertion names. Some inherited suites reuse names for different source files. Such a run can opt into a complete, ordered plan of expected source-derived invocation identities. The plan preserves every original name, result, annotation and framework flag. Add an invocation_plan object to the configuration: { "invocation_plan": { "path": "/absolute/path/invocation-plan.json", "sha256": "EXPECTED_PLAN_SHA256", "expected_invocations": 22804, "corpus_manifest": "/absolute/path/corpus-manifest.json", "corpus_manifest_sha256": "EXPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256", "corpus_root": "/absolute/path/upstream" } } expected_invocations pins the complete row count and must be positive. A count pin catches truncated plans during setup. It does not prove source correspondence. Both expected hashes must be lowercase SHA-256 values. The runner checks them before execution and parses those same verified bytes. The plan binds the configured suite, upstream revision, exact suite bytes and corpus manifest. The manifest binds every original corpus input. All physical paths are absolute. The runner assumes that no process changes input files during a run. This immutable-input assumption also applies to the existing input-hashing contract. Hash verification does not remove the race if another writer changes an input after verification. A plan uses schema gossil.invocation-plan.v1. Each row contains name and id. An ID contains suite and a structured position. Corpus positions use kind: "corpus", an upstream-relative source, a zero-based iteration and a positive slot. Empty controls use kind: "empty" with a positive index. The final framework position uses kind: "framework". For delta1, slot identifies one of the three assertions in each mutation iteration, numbered 1 through 3. The empty-control index identifies one of three final empty-input assertions, also numbered 1 through 3. The complete object shapes are shown below. These illustrative objects have one corpus row. They are not a complete plan for the real delta1 suite. Replace all hash placeholders with hashes of the exact bytes and include every real row. { "schema": "gossil.invocation-plan.v1", "suite": "delta1", "revision": "PINNED_REVISION", "suite_sha256": "SUITE_SHA256", "corpus_manifest_sha256": "MANIFEST_SHA256", "rows": [ {"name": "delta-example-0-1", "id": {"suite": "delta1", "position": { "kind": "corpus", "source": "test/example.txt", "iteration": 0, "slot": 1 }}} ] } The corresponding manifest has this shape: { "suite": "delta1", "revision": "PINNED_REVISION", "files": {"test/example.txt": "FILE_SHA256"} } Source paths use forward slashes and contain no empty, dot or parent components. IDs must be unique, and plan rows must cover every manifest source. Review of the generator and source establishes correspondence for every invocation. Hashes bind supplied bytes. Arbitrary identity labels alone do not prove provenance. The runner compares the entire observed vector with the complete expected original-name sequence and cardinality. It attaches expected_invocation_id only after an exact match. Invalid syntax remains malformed in either mode. No assertion is dropped, repaired, renamed or reordered. Failures, skipped summaries, bad totals, invalid UTF-8, nonzero exits and timeouts still reject. The report retains every plan row. The run directory also keeps exact verified invocation-plan.json and corpus-manifest.json bytes. Expected IDs describe correspondence derived from pinned source order. The original upstream log does not emit these IDs. Matching names cannot detect permutations or substitutions of whole groups with identical printed names. The frozen suite and original corpus establish their expected order. For the pinned delta1 corpus, generate the plan from the original source tree: just delta1-plan /absolute/path/fossil /absolute/path/new-plan-directory The generator uses the selected Tcl interpreter’s actual lsort order and file root behavior. lsort determines the order of corpus paths. file root removes the final filename extension to form the printed name stem. It preserves all non-directory corpus inputs and emits all 22,804 rows for 76 files, three empty controls and the framework assertion. The output directory must not exist. The source root must contain the original test/delta1.test and adjacent corpus. The recipe uses .jlog/bin/tclsh and labels the plan with revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. It does not verify the source checkout against that revision. Supply the pinned source and review its correspondence before using the plan. The generator writes invocation-plan.json, corpus-manifest.json and generation.json. Use the plan and manifest hashes from generation.json for the configuration pins. Set corpus_root to the source root. Generation metadata records the Tcl and generator hashes and complete source order. The development guide links the executed qualification evidence.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: The runner implements Unix process groups. The current checks ran on macOS, while Linux execution remains unqualified. Each invocation uses a fresh directory, a cleared environment, isolated HOME and temporary paths, and a fixed system utility PATH of /usr/bin:/bin. The runner observes completion without reaping the process-group leader. It checks the group identity before terminating owned descendants, then reaps the direct child. A timeout always rejects the run. Execution assumes trusted local programs with the same user credentials. The runner rejects setuid and setgid targets. Descendants that change their credentials, process group or session are unsupported. The runner is not a sandbox and does not promise a deadline for uninterruptible kernel work. It reaps its direct child and terminates descendants in the same process group. On macOS, XNU returns EPERM for a group containing only zombies. After the leader exits, the runner records that outcome as no-signalable-members under the trusted-program assumptions above. Other permission failures block the run. The XNU signal implementation defines that behavior.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: API: apply gives the exact contract. gossil::delta applies Fossil deltas to byte slices. A delta describes output with literal bytes and copies from an original byte slice. The library validates the commands before allocating output, then returns the decoded bytes. The gossil vcs test-delta-apply diagnostic exposes that decoder through files. It opens no repository or database and does not forward work to C Fossil.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: From the repository root, run: cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Replace ORIGIN, DELTA and TARGET with file paths. Quote paths that contain spaces. The command reads both inputs and finishes decoding before it opens TARGET. The target can be the same path as either input. On success, it writes exactly the decoded bytes, returns status 0 and leaves stdout and stderr empty. Cargo may print build messages on stderr before the executable runs. The command returns status 1 for usage, read, decode, allocation or write errors. The characterized diagnostics are: Failure Stderr line Unsupported command or argument count Usage: gossil vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Missing input no such file: PATH Delta rejection or buffer reservation failure Delta application failed. Target open or write failure unable to open file "PATH" for writing Each diagnostic ends with one LF byte, and stdout remains empty. Other input read errors include the path and the underlying I/O error. The command has no root-level test-delta-apply alias. Usage, input-read and decode failures preserve an existing target because it has not been opened. A write failure can leave a truncated or partially written target. The command does not replace files atomically.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: The decoder API exposes output_size, apply, Limits and DeltaError. The same module also exposes the encoder function create. output_size(delta) parses only the advertised output size and its LF delimiter. It does not validate the commands or enforce the output limit used by apply. use gossil::delta::{Limits, apply, output_size}; let delta = b"3\n3:ABC0;"; assert_eq!(output_size(delta).unwrap(), 3); let output = apply(b"", delta, Limits { max_output_bytes: 1024 }).unwrap(); assert_eq!(output, b"ABC"); apply(source, delta, limits) returns Result , DeltaError>. The result has exactly the advertised size, with no trailing NUL byte. Both input slices must fit within i32::MAX bytes. The output ceiling is the smaller of limits.max_output_bytes and i32::MAX. Limits::default() uses i32::MAX, as does the file diagnostic. The first pass checks command syntax, source ranges, literal lengths, cumulative output length and the final size. After validation, the decoder reserves output storage with a fallible operation and replays the checked slices in a second pass. It stores no list of parsed operations. Invalid commands reach no output reservation. An empty result needs no reservation. The decoder returns these DeltaError variants: Error variant Meaning MissingHeaderNewline Header digits are not followed by LF. InputTooLarge A source or delta input exceeds the signed-length envelope. OutputTooLarge The advertised output exceeds the effective ceiling. TruncatedCommand A numeric command has no following operator. MissingCopyComma A copy offset has no present comma delimiter. UnknownOperator An operator byte is not defined. SourceRange A copy exceeds the source, including a zero copy beyond its end. OutputRange A command would exceed the advertised output. TruncatedLiteral A literal has fewer bytes than its count. Unterminated The input ends or reaches a command-start NUL before a semicolon. SizeMismatch A semicolon arrives before the advertised output is complete. AllocationFailed Output reservation failed, with the original TryReserveError retained as its cause. Fallible reservation reports recoverable allocation failures. It does not guarantee recovery from an operating-system kill or memory exhaustion after a successful reservation.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: A delta starts with the encoded output length and LF. The form COUNT:BYTES inserts a literal, COUNT@OFFSET, copies from the source, and CHECKSUM; ends the delta. All numbers use the alphabet below. The decoder uses the exact unsigned-byte digit alphabet: 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz~ Numbers wrap modulo 2^32, and empty numeric fields mean zero. High-bit bytes are not aliases for ASCII digits or delimiters. Zero-count copies still require a valid source offset and a comma. Literal payloads can contain arbitrary bytes. The decoder requires a semicolon and an exact final output size, then ignores trailing bytes. Checksum verification is disabled, as it is in the pinned reference build. The numeric field before the semicolon is parsed but not checked against the output. Accepted wrong-checksum fixtures remain accepted. Checked ranges and slice access reject truncation at boundaries where the C implementation can read beyond its logical input. Those C pointer behaviors are not format guarantees.

title: Bounded delta encoder
text: From the repository root, replace the capitalized arguments with file paths: cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 test-delta-create reads both inputs before opening DELTA for writing. The output can share either input path. Success returns status 0 with empty stdout and stderr. test-delta creates and applies deltas in both directions, compares both results with the original bytes, and prints ok followed by LF. A failed comparison, creation or round-trip application returns status 1 with delta test failed on stderr. File-buffer reservation failures return Delta application failed.. Cargo may print build messages on stderr before the executable runs. The commands require exactly three and two paths, respectively. Usage errors return status 1 and the matching usage line. Missing inputs produce no such file: PATH. Output failures produce unable to open file "PATH" for writing. Each diagnostic ends with LF. Other read errors retain the path and underlying I/O error. Usage and input-read failures preserve an existing output. Writing can truncate an existing output before a later write fails. These diagnostics have no root command aliases. They read and write file data through paths. test-delta uses stdout only for its ok diagnostic. Reading file data from stdin, writing file data to stdout, automatic parent-folder creation and complete native I/O diagnostic parity are outside this qualification.

title: Bounded delta encoder
text: The encoder follows the pinned Fossil src/delta.c algorithm. It indexes source landmarks, scans target windows for matching source bytes, and emits copies when they cover their encoding overhead. Other bytes become literals. Its rolling hash uses sixteen signed bytes, matching the selected native build. Checksums sum unsigned big-endian four-byte words with wrapping arithmetic and right-zero padding for the last short word. Sources of at most sixteen bytes produce one literal, including a zero-length literal for an empty target. Longer sources omit that zero literal. The hash tables omit the last complete source block and visit newer landmarks first. Each target window examines at most 250 candidates. Backward extension stops before source offset zero. A match equal to its encoding overhead is accepted. Equal-length candidates retain the first visited match, and the first target window with a winning match emits it immediately. Both inputs must fit within i32::MAX bytes. The encoder counts integer digits with unsigned arithmetic. The native signed shift above 2^30 is undefined. Unsigned counting there is a safe Rust policy and does not promise giant-input native parity. Slice lengths and addresses remain bounded by existing inputs. Every output append reserves storage before extending the vector. Both hash tables also reserve before initialization. EncoderAllocationFailed records the buffer stage, requested element count and original TryReserveError cause. The source and target size checks reuse InputTooLarge. Tests exercise genuine capacity-overflow errors without asking the allocator for giant storage. Fallible reservation does not promise recovery from an operating-system kill.

title: Gest project values

Then assemble every field for conversion. Nullable archive state requires an explicit null. The converter does not read a clock, generate an identifier, look up references or execute SQL. use gossil::gest_project_values::{ProjectValueInputs, project_from_values, project_to_values}; use serde_json::json; let fields = ProjectValueInputs { gest_id: json!("kkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk"), archived_at: json!(null), created_at: json!("2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00"), updated_at: json!("2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"), }; let project = project_from_values(fields).unwrap(); let values = project_to_values(&project); assert_eq!(values.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00")); assert_eq!(project_from_values(values).unwrap(), project); The example sets modification before creation to show that conversion imposes no time ordering.

The public input and output use the same TaskValueInputs type. use gossil::gest_task_values::{TaskValueInputs, task_from_values, task_to_values}; use serde_json::json; let fields = TaskValueInputs { gest_id: json!("zyxwvutsrqponmlkzyxwvutsrqponmlk"), project_id: json!("kkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk"), title: json!("Review task values"), priority: json!(255), status: json!("IN_PROGRESS"), description: json!(""), assigned_to: json!(null), metadata: json!([null, {"reviewed": false}]), resolved_at: json!(null), created_at: json!("2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00"), updated_at: json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00Z"), }; let task = task_from_values(fields).unwrap(); let values = task_to_values(&task); assert_eq!(values.status, json!("in-progress")); assert_eq!(values.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00")); assert_eq!(task_from_values(values).unwrap(), task); The example uses array metadata and priority 255 to show the model’s full value types. Production callers must handle TaskValueError from validation. Its display text names the first rejected field and the reason, without echoing the supplied value. TaskValueError::parse_cause() returns the original chrono::ParseError when parsing the input or its canonical UTC output fails. Callers can inspect its kind() to distinguish failures such as TooShort and OutOfRange. Other validation failures return no parse cause. Error equality includes the retained cause, so errors with equal display text can compare unequal. Chrono’s alloc-only build does not implement std::error::Error for this parser error, so callers use the accessor rather than Error::source(). The validated record stays unchanged if a caller changes the owned fields returned by task_to_values.

title: Gest task values
text: The input requires all eleven fields, even when a value is null. Field Admitted value gest_id Full task ID string, called id in upstream Model. project_id Full project ID string. title Any string. priority Null or a JSON integer from 0 through 255. status A status string accepted by upstream FromStr. description Any string. assigned_to Null or a full author ID string. metadata Any serde_json::Value, including null. resolved_at A timestamp string for terminal status, otherwise null. created_at A timestamp string. updated_at A timestamp string. The task and project identifiers require exactly 32 lowercase letters from k through z. An assignee is null or a full identifier. Title and description preserve their strings, including empty strings, Unicode, whitespace and null characters. The task field gest_id corresponds to upstream Model.id. Priority is null or an integer from 0 through 255. Checked conversion rejects negative integers, larger integers, floating point values and other JSON types. The upstream task model uses Option . Its separate named priority enum covers only 0 through 4 and is outside this module. Status parsing follows upstream FromStr. The statuses are open, in-progress, done and cancelled. Parsing accepts case differences and the in-progress, in_progress and inprogress aliases. Output uses in-progress. The adopted Gossil contract requires a resolution timestamp for done and cancelled, and null for open and in-progress. The converter checks that pairing without generating a timestamp. Metadata retains every JSON value variant, including null. Explicit metadata null is model data, independent of the nulls in optional model fields. The converter preserves JSON value semantics without promising original JSON spelling, object member order or duplicate-key detection. Business timestamps use Gest’s pinned chrono 0.4.44 RFC3339 parser and normalize to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), subject to Gossil’s canonical output contract. RFC3339 is the timestamp string format used at this boundary. Output uses chrono’s RFC3339 form with the +00:00 offset and at most nine fractional digits. The parser accepts offsets, lowercase separators, a space separator, year zero and leap seconds. It truncates fractional input beyond nanoseconds, as upstream does. Business timestamp rules are separate from the stricter artifact D-card time grammar. The converter adds no ordering rule between timestamps. A parsed instant must have a UTC representation that the RFC3339 parser can read back. Offset normalization across the year zero or 9999 boundary can produce a signed extended year. The converter rejects those results under the adopted output contract. Upstream source parsing accepts their inputs. Year zero and nearby offsets remain valid when their UTC result is representable. The module does not claim parity with the full upstream timestamp input domain. Invalid field types, incomplete identifiers, invalid priorities or statuses, unparseable timestamps and inconsistent status/resolution pairs return TaskValueError. Normalized UTC output outside the adopted RFC3339 domain also returns that error. Metadata has no further type restriction.

title: Local database ownership
text: API: LocalStore gives the exact contract. The storage module opens local libSQL files and owns one write transaction at a time. Its low-level lifecycle API also supports the validated native storage boundary, which installs the complete schema and implements empty-root initialization and bounded private content operations. Opening that higher-level repository validates its stored root and authority metadata. Migration and broader adapters remain unimplemented.

title: Local database ownership
text: use gossil::storage::{LocalStore, StorageError}; async fn lifecycle(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result  { let mut store = LocalStore::open(path).await?; store.begin_write().await?.commit().await?; store.begin_write().await?.rollback().await?; Ok(()) } The example opens the database and terminates empty transactions. Use LocalOwnerRepository for admitted native content operations. The example above uses only the low-level lifecycle API. LocalStore::open(path) builds a local database and retains one connection. Every file open sets and reads back WAL, foreign keys ON, synchronous=FULL and a 5000 ms busy timeout. WAL is SQLite’s write-ahead journal mode. An open fails if configuration differs from these requirements. begin_write(&mut self) takes the connection before it issues BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The returned WriteTransaction, the transaction owner, exclusively borrows the store. A second owner cannot borrow it at the same time. There is no public SQL, connection, statement or lazy query interface. An internal execution error marks the owner rollback-only, which means later internal operations cannot issue SQL and commit must reject the operation. Queries materialize results by collecting rows into owned values before returning. They consume their statements and rows inside the owner. Preparation, stepping and value-decoding errors follow the same failure path. The native content operations also latch non-SQL failures through the owner. Fixture SQL uses the same private execution and row-collection code as the storage boundary. Explicit commit and rollback return the connection only after SQLite reports that no transaction remains active. A commit error triggers checked rollback when the transaction remains active. Errors retain the original engine cause and report a separate cleanup failure when one occurs. If commit fails but checked rollback restores an idle connection, the store can begin another write. The commit still returns its original error. A failed BEGIN or cleanup discards the connection and poisons the store. A poisoned store requires an explicit new open.

title: Local database ownership
text: Dropping a WriteTransaction without explicit termination poisons the store and drops its sole connection. The destructor executes no SQL and polls no future. The pinned local libSQL connection uses SQLite’s close_v2 API. SQLite rolls back an active transaction when the connection is destroyed. This depends on the module keeping statements and other connection aliases inside the owner. Local SQL calls block their current asynchronous poll, including busy waits. The cancellation fixture aborts at a controlled await between SQL calls and awaits task destruction before checking writer progress. Cancellation after a successful COMMIT leaves committed rows in the database. It cannot undo a commit whose result the outer caller has not received. A later server adapter must define its blocking scheduling and result-delivery boundaries.

title: Native local storage
text: LocalOwnerRepository::create exclusively creates the database file and binds its repository, owner and checkout identities. The initial root contains native C, D, R, T, U and Z records. The parser validates those bytes with date conversion on the same owned SQL connection. Creation installs all six accepted schema files, native markers, compressed root content, native crosslinks, owner, checkout and public receipt together. The final complete-policy marker follows those writes. A failed creation rolls back the schema writes. Root construction computes the encoded user length and complete canonical length before allocating either output. The size calculation and encoder use the same existing token escape rules. Private decoding boundaries check fully stepped native date values and owned catalog fields. A failure rolls back earlier writes in the transaction. Metadata errors preserve the underlying operating-system cause. LocalOwnerRepository::open requires an existing readable and writable regular file. Its explicit AdmissionLimits bound root reconstruction and parsing. Admission checks canonical bytes, native branch tags and event, the public receipt, checkout bindings, complete policy and native versions. The receipt must identify the root itself with validation class local-explicit-publication. The event fields and both branch tags must match the canonical root, including absent event overrides. Admission rejects native or valid typed projections that claim the empty root produces another artifact type or requires a graph dependency. It also rejects current file, merge, path-selection and journal rows outside the empty checkout. A producer identifies the artifact that creates a fact. A target identifies what a fact refers to. Admission distinguishes those roles rather than rejecting every row that mentions the root. Operational and provenance rows, invalid diagnostic records and historical selection records can remain. Unrelated private blobs and physical deltas can remain, including a private delta whose baseline is the public root. These rows do not extend the supported public graph or implement their corresponding product operations. AdmissionLimits bound root content reconstruction and parser allocations. Fixed scalar conflict queries bound the data they return. Neither mechanism sets a ceiling on SQLite scan work across stored tables. Operating-system access establishes the local owner boundary. A stored owner ID is a binding, and callers cannot turn an ID string into permission. shared_view() returns a restricted local view with no owner operations. Network authentication and team principals remain unimplemented. The shared view reads the initial public root only. An absent name and a private file name return the same unavailable error. A private association with already public root bytes preserves their public classification. A receipt for an unsupported general graph cannot grant shared access.

title: Native local storage
text: Admission is the validation required before repository operations. A sealed admission proof records SQLite data_version, connection total_changes and exact durable authority metadata. Each content operation checks that proof under its writer reservation before a private lookup. The saved metadata includes the root-conflict predicates. Refreshing only the connection counter cannot accept a newly contradictory projection. An unrelated external commit conservatively requires explicit readmission. Unexpected writes on the same connection also require readmission. Supported private file operations refresh only total_changes after checked commit or rollback. They preserve the admitted root and policy, and they never advance the saved data_version. Future root or policy mutation APIs must invalidate or replace the proof after full validation. Content operations do not decode the root through a hidden admission budget. They check durable authority and charge requested content to caller limits. Creation and open use their separate, explicit admission limits.

title: Native local storage
text: Use put_private_file_content to store private bytes and read_content to retrieve them through LocalOwnerRepository. Every content read or write receives finite Limits. Those limits bound each stored envelope, decoded output, chain depth and aggregate stored and decoded work. Reconstruction checks every intermediate native size and full hash. A RID is a native artifact row identifier. A visited-RID set rejects cycles. A phantom is an artifact whose content is missing. Shunned artifacts are excluded by repository policy. Missing, phantom and shunned baselines reject successful reconstruction. The four-byte big-endian envelope retains native codec behavior. Excess capacity and bytes after the first complete zlib stream are accepted. Exact repository size and hash still have to match. A short NoPayload result cannot stand in for valid empty content. compression::pack_bounded uses the existing encoder and checks the full stored length before each output reservation. Its ceiling includes the header. The encoder also uses a fixed 8192-byte working buffer and backend state. The ceiling is not a bound on every allocation in the process. A hash, policy, codec, schema or resource error makes the borrowed owner rollback-only. Catching the error cannot permit later SQL or successful commit. Earlier writes in that transaction also roll back. Full bytes can replace a phantom or a delta target whose old baseline is missing. Replacement removes the stale delta row and clears phantom state. Typed dependents are records in the adapter projections that require the content. Required orphan, delta or typed dependents cause an explicit refusal until their native and typed crosslinks are implemented.

title: Native local storage
text: The complete schema comes from six SQL files under src/storage/schema/. The required object inventory and complete stored definitions are checked before mutation. Known optional schema families return an unsupported configuration error. Unregistered persistent triggers receive a separate error. Dynamic ticket templates, extension schemas and their registry transitions remain unimplemented. General public receipts, publication, native and typed rebuild, retained-dependency administration and filesystem journals also remain unimplemented. The public APIs do not offer those operations.

title: Fossil token bytes
text: API: fossilize gives the exact contract. The gossil::token_codec module encodes and decodes arbitrary bytes for Fossil artifact and protocol tokens. It implements the token escape functions from Fossil revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6, src/encode.c:392-458. It does not parse artifacts or select repository hash policy.

title: Fossil token bytes
text: All three functions return Result and preserve allocation error causes. fossilize encodes the entire slice, including embedded NUL bytes. fossilize_c_string encodes bytes before the first NUL, or the whole slice when no NUL occurs. Both return bytes without a C terminator. The eight escaped bytes are NUL, space, tab, newline, carriage return, vertical tab, form feed and backslash. Their escape letters are 0, s, t, n, r, v, f and backslash. Each follows a backslash. Other bytes pass through unchanged. No function requires UTF-8. defossilize stops reading at the first source NUL or the slice end. Unknown escapes discard the backslash. For example, \q decodes to q. A terminal backslash survives. The returned DecodedToken.bytes contains every emitted byte, including bytes emitted after a decoded NUL. Its c_string_len is the first decoded NUL index, or the output length. C-string consumers see only that prefix. use gossil::token_codec::{defossilize, fossilize}; let encoded = fossilize(b"a b\0").unwrap(); let decoded = defossilize(&encoded).unwrap(); assert_eq!(decoded.bytes, b"a b\0"); assert_eq!(decoded.c_string_len, 3); The implementation checks the exact encoded size and reserves output storage before emitting bytes. TokenError::Size rejects arithmetic overflow or lengths above Rust vector capacity. TokenError::Allocation retains the allocator error. These errors are Rust resource policies. The C comparison requires valid pointers, terminated C strings and explicit lengths within allocated storage. It excludes signed C integer overflow and allocation exhaustion.

This module does not admit migration or implement the Gest API. task_from_values validates the eleven explicit TaskValueInputs fields. task_to_values recovers them from the private TaskValues record with canonical status spelling and UTC timestamp strings. Business timestamps use chrono 0.4.44 parsing, then reject normalized output that cannot be parsed again. They do not use the artifact D-card grammar or impose timestamp ordering.

A null Value is data for metadata and marks absence for nullable fields. Validate this input with task_from_values before using it as a task record. Parameter Type Description task &TaskValues A record validated by [task_from_values]. returns TaskValueInputs Eleven explicit owned values.
